title: Alma takes up the teaching
summary: After Amulek silences Zeezrom, Alma begins to speak to him before the surrounding multitude, establishing Amulek’s words and unfolding the scriptures further.

explicit_facts.text: Alma sees that Amulek's words have silenced Zeezrom, who trembles under awareness of his guilt.
Alma opens his mouth and begins speaking to Zeezrom, establishing Amulek's words and explaining the scriptures further.
The multitude hears Alma's words; it is great in number.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and Zeezrom are positioned so Alma can address him.
The multitude is gathered within hearing distance.
unspecified_visual_details: The precise location, clothing, ages, and arrangement of the crowd.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show any unseen prior exchange as a present action.

title: Alma exposes Zeezrom’s plan
summary: Alma addresses Zeezrom and the people, declaring that Zeezrom lied to God and describing his plan to turn the people against Alma and Amulek. He calls it a snare of the adversary.

explicit_facts.text: Alma tells Zeezrom that he lied to God and that his thoughts are known through God's Spirit.
Alma describes Zeezrom's plan to turn the people against Alma and Amulek and have them reviled and cast out.
Alma says the plan was of Zeezrom's adversary and tells the gathered people to remember his words.
Alma calls the plan a snare meant to bring the people into subjection and everlasting destruction.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma speaks audibly to Zeezrom and the gathered people.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible manifestation of the adversary, chains, or a snare.

spoken_dialogue.text: Now Zeezrom, seeing that thou hast been taken in thy lying and craftiness, for thou hast not lied unto men only but thou hast lied unto God;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma (son of Alma)

spoken_dialogue.text: Now I would that ye should remember that what I say unto thee I say unto all.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma (son of Alma)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The chains and snare are figurative teaching, not literal visible objects.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the devil or literal chains as present.

title: Zeezrom trembles and asks
summary: Zeezrom trembles more and becomes convinced of God's power and Alma and Amulek's knowledge of his heart. He diligently asks Alma about resurrection and judgment.

explicit_facts.text: Zeezrom trembles more exceedingly and is convinced of God's power and of Alma and Amulek's knowledge of his thoughts and intents.
Zeezrom diligently inquires about the kingdom of God and asks Alma what Amulek meant concerning resurrection and judgment according to works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Zeezrom visibly trembles as he addresses Alma.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible supernatural sign or depiction of Zeezrom's thoughts.

spoken_dialogue.text: What does this mean which Amulek hath spoken concerning the resurrection of the dead, that all shall rise from the dead, both the just and the unjust, and are brought to stand before God to be judged according to their works?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Zeezrom

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Do not depict resurrection or judgment as a current event; Zeezrom asks about them.
prohibited_inventions: Do not visualize thoughts as readable images or symbols.

title: The portion of the word
summary: Alma explains that knowledge of God's mysteries is given according to heed and diligence. Those who harden their hearts receive less, while those who do not harden their hearts may come to know the mysteries in full.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says many may know God's mysteries but are commanded to impart only according to the portion granted, based on heed and diligence.
Alma contrasts the lesser portion given to the hard-hearted with the greater portion given to those who do not harden their hearts.
Alma says the hard-hearted may lose knowledge of the mysteries and be taken captive; he identifies this as the chains of hell.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues speaking to Zeezrom while the multitude listens.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visual form for knowledge, mysteries, captivity, or chains.

narration.text: It is given unto many to know the mysteries of God;
And they that will harden their hearts, to them is given the lesser portion of the word

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Chains of hell and captivity are figurative teaching here, not a literal scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a supernatural captor or literal chains.

title: Death and judgment
summary: Alma teaches that people will be raised from mortality to immortality and judged according to their works. He warns of condemnation and says all must stand before God and acknowledge his just judgments.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says people will be raised from mortality to immortality and judged according to their works.
He warns that hardened hearts will bring condemnation, and that words, works, and thoughts will condemn.
He says all must stand before God and acknowledge the justice of his judgments and his mercy toward the children of men.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma speaks to Zeezrom and the gathered people.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of God, a judgment setting, or any resurrected person.

narration.text: we must come forth and stand before him in his glory,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is teaching about future judgment, not a present judgment scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show God or a resurrection as a current visible event.

title: The second death
summary: Alma describes spiritual death for those who die in their sins, teaching that their torments will be like a lake of fire and brimstone and that they cannot be redeemed according to God's justice.

explicit_facts.text: Alma describes a second, spiritual death for those who die in their sins.
He compares their torments to a lake of fire and brimstone and says they will be chained to everlasting destruction.
He says they cannot be redeemed according to God's justice and cannot die, as there is no more corruption.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues the teaching before the listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: Any literal lake, flame, chains, or persons experiencing torment.

narration.text: Then, I say unto you, they shall be as though there had been no redemption made;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The lake of fire and chains are figures in Alma's teaching, not a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal hellscape, flames, or Satan.

title: Antionah questions Alma
summary: After Alma finishes speaking, the people become more astonished. Antionah, a chief ruler among them, comes forth and questions Alma about rising from the dead and the scripture concerning Eden.

explicit_facts.text: Alma finishes speaking, and the people begin to be more astonished.
Antionah is a chief ruler among them and comes forth to speak to Alma.
Antionah asks about rising from the dead and changing from a mortal to an immortal state.
Antionah asks about scripture concerning cherubim and a flaming sword east of the garden of Eden, then says there was no possible chance that the first parents should live forever.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Antionah stands forward of the people while addressing Alma.

spoken_dialogue.text: What is this that thou hast said, that man should rise from the dead and be changed from this mortal to an immortal state that the soul can never die?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Antionah

spoken_dialogue.text: And thus we see that there was no possible chance that they should live forever.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Antionah

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Antionah mentions Eden while questioning scripture; the verses do not place the present exchange there.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the first parents, cherubim, or flaming sword as present in this exchange.
Do not invent additional speech or a response from Alma.

title: The Fall and mortality
summary: Alma explains that Adam fell by partaking of the forbidden fruit and that mankind became fallen. He teaches that death came upon mankind, while this life provides a time to repent and prepare to meet God.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says Adam fell by partaking of the forbidden fruit and all mankind became a lost and fallen people.
Alma says that if Adam had partaken of the tree of life then, there would have been no death and God's word would have been void.
Alma teaches that temporal death comes to mankind and that life is a probationary state and time to prepare to meet God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma answers Antionah before the gathered audience.
unspecified_visual_details: Adam, the forbidden fruit, or the tree of life as visible figures or objects in this present moment.

narration.text: Adam did fall by the partaking of the forbidden fruit,
this life became a probationary state;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Alma recounts and explains past events; do not turn these into flashback scenes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage Adam's act or Eden as a current visual moment.

title: The plan of redemption
summary: Alma teaches that the plan of redemption makes resurrection possible. He says that without a preparatory state, partaking of the tree of life would have frustrated the plan, and that death is appointed before judgment.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says the plan of redemption, laid from the foundation of the world, brings about resurrection.
He says that living forever without a preparatory state would have frustrated the plan of redemption.
Alma says it is appointed that people die and after death come to judgment.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues teaching to Antionah and the assembled audience.
unspecified_visual_details: A visual representation of the plan, resurrection, or future judgment.

narration.text: there was a plan of redemption laid,

title: Angels and the plan made known

explicit_facts.text: God saw it was expedient that people know what he had appointed for them.
God sent angels to converse with people, causing them to behold his glory.
People began to call on God's name; God conversed with them and made the plan known according to their faith, repentance, and holy works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma speaks to Antionah and the listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity or appearance of the angels, the people addressed, and God's appearance.

title: Commandments and agency
summary: Alma teaches that after people transgressed the first commandments and became able to know good from evil, God gave commandments and warned that evil brings a second death.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says people first transgressed commandments concerning temporal things and came to know good from evil, able to act according to their wills.
God gave commandments after making the plan of redemption known, warning against evil and its second-death penalty.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma continues his explanation to the assembled listeners.
unspecified_visual_details: The first transgression, any specific commandment scene, or a visible second death.

title: Mercy through the Only Begotten Son
summary: Alma recounts God's call to repent and not harden the heart, promising mercy and remission of sins through his Only Begotten Son to the repentant, while warning the hard-hearted will not enter his rest.

explicit_facts.text: Alma says God called on people in the name of his Son, promising mercy through his Only Begotten Son to those who repent and do not harden their hearts.
Those who repent and do not harden their hearts may claim mercy and remission of sins and enter God's rest.
Those who harden their hearts and do iniquity will not enter God's rest.

title: Alma calls the people to repent
summary: Alma warns his brethren against hardening their hearts and urges them to repent and enter the rest of God rather than provoke the Lord's wrath.

explicit_facts.text: Alma warns his brethren that hardening their hearts and iniquity will keep them from the Lord's rest and bring destruction.
Alma urges them to repent, not harden their hearts, and enter the rest of God.
